newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index down at noon on A share fall.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index down at noon on A share fall.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index edged lower by midday on Tuesday, dragged down by falls in A shares and property stocks, analysts said.
The foreign currency B index lost 1.42 points or 0.80 percent to 175.12 on turnover of HK$84.29 million.
"Substantial losses in the A share market soured the mood of B share investors," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
The domestic currency A share index slid 6.64 points or 1.36 percent to 481.61 due to a correction, analysts said. Turnover was 8.6 billion yuan.
"But the B index is unlikely to fall sharply as it has found support at current levels," the Guotai analyst said.
Heavy selling of property shares also weighed on the B index, making investors cautious in the last two days of the annual results reporting season, brokers said.
Companies must report 1996 results by April 30.
SEZ Real Estate fell to its 10 percent daily limit-down in early morning trading for the second straight session after announcing poor 1996 annual results over the weekend.
The stock recovered slightly by noon, ending at HK$3.83, down HK$0.24 or 5.90 percent on volume of 1.61 million shares.
The company posted a net loss of 26.34 million yuan for 1996 based on international accounting standards.
"People did not expect such bad results from SEZ," an analyst at J&A Securities said. "But the selling has slowed after sharp declines."
SEZ Real Estate was also among the biggest losers in the A share market, tumbling 0.75 yuan or 6.44 percent to 10.89 yuan.
